topics.name: Bayesian optimization and adaptive experimentation
topics.summary: Multi-fidelity transfer, elite-candidate generation, threshold-agnostic Bayesian search, photonics design, creative testing, and materials discovery frame experiments as costly sequential decisions. Learned surrogates, recovery paths, and adaptive acquisition reduce evaluations while preserving useful exploration.

topics.name: Theory and algorithms for optimization
topics.summary: Theoretical work analyzes learning regimes, sparse-network routing, convergence certificates, evolutionary population sizes, constrained search, symbolic regression, and moment estimation. Across these settings, explicit rate bounds and structural assumptions clarify when an optimizer can scale or generalize.

topics.name: Clinical biosignal and physiological prediction
topics.summary: PPG, ECG, EEG, bone measurements, and motion-capture studies compare deep pipelines, interpretable waveform features, masked pretraining, and cross-device validation. Results favor multimodal or harmonized signals for robust clinical prediction while highlighting dataset and measurement variability.

topics.name: Pathology and medical image analysis
topics.summary: Medical vision papers address Gleason grading, glioblastoma radiomics, whole-slide token selection, multi-scale pathology, long-tailed classification, and EEG-guided prosthetic vision. Weak labels, sequential evidence selection, and robustness analyses seek clinically useful detail without assuming balanced or pristine data.

topics.name: Formal specification and verified reasoning
topics.summary: Execution-grounded specification benchmarks, Lean formalization, FastLAS instruction, quantum-field claim repair, executable contracts, and metamorphic spatial tests connect language outputs to checkable semantics. The studies show that running or mechanically validating generated artifacts is stronger than judging plausibility by text alone.

topics.name: Multilingual language reasoning and communication
topics.summary: Language studies compare riddles, debate behavior, legal QA, visual-text interpretation, offensive-language transfer, phonetic features, instruction hierarchy, and citation language across cultures and scripts. The findings link reasoning quality to linguistic context, annotation choices, and the structure of the evidence shown to a model.

topics.name: Agent safety, evaluation, and coordination
topics.summary: Agent studies probe chain-of-thought failure, multimodal fact checking, delegation, authority, tool-use benchmarks, API routing, frozen-model claims, and inter-agent protocols. They treat permissions, evidence, and resource costs as first-class evaluation targets rather than relying on answer accuracy alone.

topics.name: Reinforcement learning for agents and long-horizon tasks
topics.summary: Reinforcement-learning work improves sparse-reward reasoning, visual-agent critics, and long-horizon manipulation through curriculum design, advantage estimation, outcome-aware supervision, and self-verifiable rewards. Memory and distillation mechanisms aim to reuse successful procedures without erasing exploration.

topics.name: Autonomous vehicle and UAV safety planning
topics.summary: Autonomous-driving and aerial-robot studies combine multimodal perception, risk-aware reinforcement learning, trajectory tracking, off-road traversability, drifting control, and policy-compliance benchmarks. Simulations and real vehicle settings emphasize degraded observations, dynamic clutter, energy limits, and operational rules.

topics.name: Embodied manipulation and tactile world models
topics.summary: Robot-control papers use polynomial motor models, curriculum learning, adjacent-action prediction, language guidance, tactile tokens, and contact-rich world models for manipulation. The shared goal is to ground policies in physical interaction so they remain useful beyond a single scripted trajectory.

topics.name: Multimodal perception and remote sensing
topics.summary: Vision systems cover object re-identification, adverse-weather driving, infrared fusion, event-based depth, PolSAR classification, road reconstruction, sonar augmentation, aerial tracking, and disaster geolocation. Cross-modal features and physically informed geometry improve recognition when viewpoint, weather, or sensing modality changes.

topics.name: Generative media and expressive avatars
topics.summary: Generative-media work covers physics-aware video, architectural scenes, latent concept erasure, anthropometric and head avatars, diffusion audio, evolutionary life-like media, and joint audio-video synthesis. Conditioning, explicit geometry, and cross-modal alignment are used to improve control and temporal consistency.

topics.name: Efficient LLM serving and continual adaptation
topics.summary: Serving and adaptation studies compress event-KV memory, approximate transformers homomorphically, route requests by workload, manage relational queries, and update models with low-rank or merged adapters. They report lower latency, memory, or privacy cost while tracking the risk of forgetting or refusal collapse.

topics.name: Recommender systems and semantic ranking
topics.summary: Recommendation papers address causally aligned long-term memory, music and live-stream agents, manifold-aware sequential prediction, claw-native interaction, semantic IDs, and positional attacks on listwise ranking. Efficient item representations and order-robust scoring are central to improving personalization and trust.

topics.name: Retrieval-augmented knowledge and document systems
topics.summary: Information-access studies build relevance posteriors, source-aware misinformation checks, legal corpus analysis, multimodal graph retrieval, end-to-end RAG tests, and executable spatiotemporal knowledge graphs. They stress evidence coverage, document structure, and repeatable testing as safeguards against plausible but unsupported answers.

topics.name: AI governance, privacy, and hardware security
topics.summary: Governance and security papers examine autonomy levels, political alignment, mission assurance, screen-collusion watermarking, secure code, and hardware Trojan detection. Their common message is that permissions, provenance, and runtime controls must be audited alongside model capability.

topics.name: Temporal graphs and nonstationary forecasting
topics.summary: Graph and forecasting methods model switched dynamics, imputation under changing conditions, sports outcomes, temporal events, solar irradiance, decentralized rank regression, and image-based weather signals. Adaptive dependencies and graph structure help preserve predictions when observations drift or arrive irregularly.

topics.name: Scientific machine learning and materials modeling
topics.summary: Scientific ML papers use Fourier operators, physics-informed networks, attention, molecule-language models, battery literature mining, carbon-storage surrogates, and nitrous-oxide flux constraints. The applications share a need to blend sparse observations with governing structure and uncertainty-aware simulation.

topics.name: Speech, diarization, and audio interaction
topics.summary: Audio work develops affect interpretation, psychological-support dialogue, voice-conversion identity recovery, multilingual diarization, financial-call ASR, audio equalization, and repair detection. Benchmarks and semantic or articulatory features connect acoustic robustness with interpretable conversational behavior.

topics.name: 3D geometry and articulated human representations
topics.summary: Geometric studies learn minimal surfaces, anthropometric heads, sketch and portrait meshes, dynamic hair, and articulated pose representations. Explicit geometry and temporal routing make human or object shape estimates more stable and controllable than appearance-only prediction.

topics.name: Uncertainty calibration and robust learning
topics.summary: Ordinal regression, attribution regularization, last-layer ensembles, implicit ensemble temperature, and noisy-label mixing study how models express uncertainty or resist corrupted supervision. The experiments favor explicit diversity and evidence consistency over a single confidence score.

topics.name: Datasets and human-centered AI studies
topics.summary: Dataset and user-facing studies create resources for gait identity, counseling, laboratory-robot failures, driving style, media credibility, social LLM behavior, photo archives, and conference history. Their empirical value comes from realistic interaction traces, ethical release choices, and domain-specific annotation rather than scale alone.

topics.name: Wireless communication and image compression
topics.summary: Communication studies address semantic MIMO refinement, XL-RIS channel recovery, trainable transform bases, and image coding. Learned representations are shaped around channel sparsity, rate limits, or reconstruction quality to reduce transmission cost without losing task-relevant structure.

topics.name: Statistical learning and decision theory
topics.summary: Theoretical papers cover semiparametric tangent spaces, PAC learnability, degradation-trajectory bounds, bandit complexity, graph inner products, weight decay, and quantized Fourier coefficients. They use counterexamples, sharp sample limits, and asymptotic analysis to identify where intuitive generalization claims fail.

topics.name: Surgical and single-cell decision support
topics.summary: Clinical decision-support work adapts SAM-style segmentation to surgical concepts and uses an agentic framework to identify interpretable therapeutic targets from single-cell RNA sequencing. Both cases combine domain structure with selective evidence to make specialized predictions more stable and actionable.

topics.name: Pose tracking and spatial memory for embodied systems
topics.summary: Robotic perception papers improve recoverable 6D tracking, physics-aware pose fusion, and language-conditioned re-perception over a vision-language-motion map. Their shared strategy is to retain spatial context and recover from occlusion or viewpoint change during closed-loop behavior.

topics.name: Dependency discovery in tabular data
topics.summary: Two data-management studies extend dependency discovery with efficient order handling and probabilistic functional-dependency support. Their algorithms make schema-level structure usable when observations are incomplete or uncertainty should be reported rather than hidden.

topics.name: Reinforcement learning for adaptive control
topics.summary: These reinforcement-learning studies use structured Q-functions, procedure memory, local distillation, and distributed UAV routing to improve exploration or reuse across episodes. The results connect reward design and reusable experience with better performance under sparse feedback and changing missions.

topics.name: Industrial fault diagnosis and anomaly detection
topics.summary: Industrial monitoring papers combine dynamic fuzzy weighting, differentially private online optimization, and cross-modal reconstruction matching for transformer faults or anomalous signals. They target reliable alerts with limited labels and changing operating conditions rather than idealized stationary data.
